new_technologies.title: The Last Six Months in LLMs in Five Minutes

new_technologies.description: A new Datasette plugin that works with datasette-llm and datasette-llm-accountant to configure per-user or global spending limits for LLM usage inside Datasette. Configuration example shows rolling 24-hour window with $1.00 per user daily limit. Also includes updates about tool availability permissions and background agent tools.

Microsoft is shifting developers to GitHub Copilot CLI.

Includes MCP server for integration with Cursor and Claude Desktop.

new_technologies.description: Research paper demonstrates a technique to compile agentic workflow patterns directly into LLM weights, achieving near-frontier performance at two orders of magnitude lower computational cost. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.

new_technologies.description: Large-scale collaboration demonstrating AI systems (including Aja Huang) advancing mathematics research through automated formal proof search. Represents significant progress in AI-assisted mathematical discovery. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.

new_technologies.title: Datasette Agent: First release of extensible AI assistant for Datasette
new_technologies.description: Simon Willison announced Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that integrates his LLM Python library (3 years in development) with Datasette. Features include 'View SQL query' buttons for charts, improved handling of truncated responses, and support for Datasette Agent plugins running in Fly Sprites sandbox.

new_technologies.title: Anthropic paying SpaceX $1.25 billion per month for GPU compute capacity
new_technologies.description: SpaceX S-1 filing reveals Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II GPU compute capacity. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreement terminable with 90 days notice.
new_technologies.author: Simon Willison

new_technologies.title: How fast is 10 tokens per second? Interactive simulation tool
new_technologies.description: Mike Veerman built an HTML app that simulates LLM token output speeds from 5/second to 800/second, helping developers understand what different token rates actually feel like in practice.
new_technologies.author: Simon Willison

others.title: Elon Musk loses lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI
others.description: A court has ruled in favor of Sam Altman and OpenAI in Elon Musk's lawsuit, which alleged that OpenAI betrayed its original mission as a non-profit organization. The verdict represents a significant legal victory for OpenAI and validates its transition to a capped-profit model. The case has been closely watched as a test of whether AI companies can balance mission-driven origins with commercial scaling.
others.author: Tim Fernholz

others.title: AI for Auto-Research: Roadmap & User Guide
others.description: ArXiv paper presenting a comprehensive roadmap and user guide for using AI systems to automate research processes. The paper covers frameworks for leveraging LLMs and AI agents in literature review, experiment design, data analysis, and paper writing. This represents the growing field of AI-augmented research tools and methodologies.
others.author: Lingdong Kong, Xian Sun, Wei Chow, et al.

others.title: Scalable Environments Drive Generalizable Agents
others.description: ArXiv paper investigating how scalable training environments contribute to developing more generalizable AI agents. The research suggests that diverse, large-scale environments are key to training agents that can adapt to new tasks and domains. This has implications for training AI coding agents and other agentic systems that need to generalize across different programming tasks and environments.
others.author: Jiayi Zhang, Fanqi Kong, Guibin Zhang, et al.

others.title: SkillGenBench: Benchmarking Skill Generation Pipelines for LLM Agents
others.description: ArXiv paper introducing SkillGenBench, a new benchmark for evaluating skill generation in LLM-based agents. The benchmark focuses on assessing how well AI agents can acquire and combine new skills to solve complex tasks. This is particularly relevant for AI coding agents that need to learn new programming skills and techniques dynamically.
others.author: Yifan Zhou, Zhentao Zhang, Ziming Cheng, et al.

others.title: Alignment pretraining: AI discourse creates self-fulfilling (mis)alignment
others.description: ArXiv paper exploring how public discourse about AI alignment and safety can itself influence AI development trajectories, potentially creating self-fulfilling prophecies. The paper examines the relationship between AI safety narratives, research funding priorities, and actual technical work on alignment. This meta-analysis of AI discourse is relevant to understanding how discussions about AI coding safety evolve.
others.author: Various

others.title: '11 AI agents' is meaningless as a phrase
others.description: Boris Mann quote highlighted by Simon: 'If I said "I have 11 spreadsheets" or "I have 11 browser tabs" to do my work, it means about the same thing.' Critiques the vague terminology around AI agents and calls for more precise definitions and metrics when discussing agentic systems.
others.author: Simon Willison (quoting Boris Mann)

others.title: How Claude Code Works in Large Codebases - Hacker News Discussion
others.description: A highly upvoted Hacker News discussion (241 points) about how Claude Code operates in large codebases, with community insights on AI-assisted programming workflows and best practices for working with AI coding tools at scale.
others.author: Hacker News Community

others.title: I Believe There Are Entire Companies Right Now Under AI Psychosis - Mitchell Hashimoto
others.description: Mitchell Hashimoto's tweet about 'AI psychosis' became the most upvoted story on Hacker News (1854 points), sparking intense discussion about the current state of AI adoption, hype cycles, and whether companies are making irrational decisions around AI technology.
others.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

others.title: Programming Languages Are Increasingly Fungible in the Era of Coding Agents
others.description: Simon Willison discussed how coding agents are making programming languages less about lock-in and more interchangeable. Citing Mitchell Hashimoto's comments on Bun porting from Zig to Rust: 'Programming languages used to be LOCK IN, and they're increasingly not so.' Willison shared a story about a company using coding agents to rewrite both iOS and Android apps to React Native.
others.author: Simon Willison / Mitchell Hashimoto

others.title: Bun Rust Rewrite: Codebase Fails Basic Miri Checks, Allows for UB in Safe Rust
others.description: A Hacker News discussion (464 points) about Bun's Rust rewrite, with users pointing out that the codebase 'fails basic miri checks and allows for UB (undefined behavior) in safe Rust.' This sparked debate about the safety trade-offs in rapid development with AI assistance.
others.author: Hacker News Community

others.title: Three Types of Programmers in 2026 - Context Window Management as Key Skill
others.description: Andrej Karpathy discussed how the role of programmers is evolving in 2026, with context window management becoming a key skill. He emphasizes that 'what's in the context window is your lever over the interpreter, that is the LLM.' This highlights the shift from traditional coding to context engineering.
others.author: Andrej Karpathy

others.title: Software 3.0: Programming Paradigm Shift Around Prompts
others.description: Andrej Karpathy promoted the concept of 'Software 3.0' - a new programming layer built around prompts rather than traditional code. He explains this is not just another developer tool but a fundamental shift in how programming works, moving from code to prompts as the primary abstraction.
others.author: Andrej Karpathy

others.title: Vibe Coding is the Future - Amjad Masad on Moonshots Podcast
others.description: Amjad Masad discussed why 'vibe coding' is not just a trend but the future of programming, sharing insights on AI coding impact on engineering teams and the post-coding AI era. He emphasized that this approach represents a fundamental shift in how software will be built.
others.author: Amjad Masad

others.title: Karpathy's Dramatic Shift in Coding Workflow: From 80% Manual to AI-First
others.description: Andrej Karpathy revealed a dramatic shift in his programming workflow 'in just a few weeks' due to improved LLM coding capabilities. He moved from '80% manual+autocomplete coding and 20% agents' to a much more AI-assisted approach, demonstrating how rapidly AI coding tools are evolving.
others.author: Jason Guo / Andrej Karpathy

others.title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
others.description: Coverage of UK Government Digital Service's response to NHS closing open source repositories. GDS recommends keeping open by default, warning that making everything private adds costs and reduces reuse and scrutiny. Discusses AI, open code, and vulnerability risk in the public sector.
others.author: Simon Willison

others.title: Coding agents make programming languages increasingly fungible
others.description: Discussion of how coding agents have changed the lock-in dynamics of programming languages. Cites example of company using AI to rewrite apps to React Native, and Mitchell Hashimoto's observation about Bun migrating from Zig to Rust. Programming languages used to be LOCK IN, and they're increasingly not so.
others.author: Simon Willison

others.title: Karpathy: AI is suddenly writing most of my code
others.description: According to Reddit discussions, Karpathy mentioned that 'AI is suddenly writing most of his code' and he is 'starting to atrophy' his ability to write code himself, highlighting the rapid shift in software development practices.
others.author: Andrej Karpathy

others.title: FTC Settles with Cox Media Group Over Deceptive 'Active Listening' AI Marketing Claims
others.description: FTC requires Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million to settle charges they deceived customers about 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing service. The companies claimed their service listened to consumer conversations through smart devices, but the service did not actually listen in on conversations or use voice data. Instead, they resold email lists from other data brokers at a significant markup. FTC clarified that clicking through mandatory terms of service does not constitute 'opt-in consent' for invasive data collection.
others.author: Simon Willison

others.title: UK Government Digital Service Weighs in on NHS Open Source Decision
others.description: The Government Digital Service (GDS) published 'AI, open code and vulnerability risk in the public sector' on May 14th, responding to the NHS's decision to close down access to their open source repositories. Key recommendation: 'Keep open by default. Making everything private adds additional delivery and policy costs, and can reduce reuse and scrutiny. Openness should remain the default posture, with closure used sparingly and deliberately.' Terence Eden interprets this as a major escalation in civil service terms.
others.author: Simon Willison

others.title: Hacker News Discussion: Runtime - Sandboxed Coding Agents for Teams
others.description: Launch HN: Runtime (YC P26) - Sandboxed coding agents for everyone on a team. The discussion covers 84 points with 22 comments, focusing on the approach of providing sandboxed AI coding assistants that can be used across entire teams rather than individual developers.
others.author: Hacker News

others.title: Google's Antigravity Bait and Switch
others.description: Hacker News discussion with 654 points and 298 comments about Google's transition from open source Gemini CLI (Apache 2.0 licensed TypeScript) to closed source Antigravity CLI. The discussion covers concerns about Google's changing stance on open source tools for AI development.
others.author: Hacker News

others.title: Multi-Stream LLMs: New Paper on Parallelizing Prompts, Thinking, I/O
others.description: Hacker News discussion (100 points, 12 comments) about a new arXiv paper on Multi-Stream LLMs that explores parallelizing and separating prompts, thinking, and input/output operations. This represents an architectural approach to improving LLM performance and efficiency.
others.author: Hacker News

others.title: The Memory Shortage and AI: HBM Impact on Consumer Electronics
others.description: Simon highlighted David Oks' explanation of how AI data centers are causing memory shortages. With only three major memory manufacturers and fixed wafer capacity, HBM (high-bandwidth memory for GPUs) allocation is increasing from 2% to 20% by end of 2026. Since HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR, this is causing consumer electronics to become more expensive.
others.author: Simon Willison

others.title: Ask HN: Anyone struggling to get value out of coding LLMs?
others.description: Hacker News discussion exploring developer frustration after deep testing of AI coding tools. Community discusses real-world experiences with LLM coding assistants and the gap between hype and practical value.
others.author: Hacker News community

others.title: AI can code, but it can't build software
others.description: Popular Hacker News discussion highlighting the distinction: 'LLMs are remarkably good at writing code. Writing code isn't the same thing as delivering working software.' Explores the gap between code generation and software delivery.
others.author: Hacker News community

others.title: Ask HN: Go deep into AI/LLMs or just use them as tools?
others.description: Discussion on whether developers should specialize in AI/LLMs or just use them as productivity tools. Community debates career strategy in the age of AI assistants.

others.title: Memory shortage causing repricing of consumer electronics due to AI GPU demand
others.description: David Oks explains how AI data center growth is pushing HBM (high-bandwidth memory) allocation from 2% to 20% of wafer capacity by end of 2026. Since HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR, this is constraining consumer RAM production. Expected to impact sub-$100 smartphone market particularly hard.
others.author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

others.title: FTC settles charges over deceptive 'active listening' AI marketing claims
others.description: FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million for falsely claiming their 'Active Listening' service used smart devices to listen to conversations for ad targeting. In reality, the service just resold email lists from other data brokers at markup. FTC clarified that clicking through terms of service does not constitute adequate consent for voice data collection.

He noted that AI is now writing most of his code and he is 'starting to atrophy my ability to write code manually'.
